notes: Receipt, `python tools/bib_to_lab.py`, 2026-07-24: bib entries parsed 60; evidence nodes 60; pdfs in corpus 90; pdfs linked 55; pdfs with no entry 35.
91 PDF files exist but only 90 distinct basenames: `2009_predictive_coding_under_the_free_energy_princ.pdf` appears twice on disk.
Folder layout is not uniform. P2026 holds its 40 PDFs flat; P2022/P2023/P2024/P2025 each nest theirs one level down in a bare year subdirectory. bib_to_lab.py uses rglob for this reason.

P-folder does not mean publication year. P2024 contains a `2025/` subdirectory holding a 2021 paper; P2025 contains a `2024/` subdirectory holding a 2024 paper. Observation, not yet explained â€” the folders may record acquisition date rather than publication date.
P2026 mixes two filename conventions: `<year>_<title-slug>.pdf` and `<Surname><Year>.pdf`. Several files appear under both, which is where a large share of the 35 unmatched PDFs comes from.
issues: papers.bib contains `@article{Friston_2009}` twice, byte-identical in key and title. BibTeX will warn on the repeated key and most tools keep only one. It surfaces in the graph as two nodes, evidence-friston-2009 and evidence-fristonb-2009, because the generator disambiguates rather than silently dropping. Deduplicate the bib, then re-run.

35 PDFs have no bib entry (was 44 before slug matching was corrected). Some are genuine duplicates under the second naming convention; some are papers never entered into the bibliography. Not yet separated.

`@article{1999, ...}` has a bare year as its cite key and no author field; it maps to evidence-anon-1999 and corresponds on disk to `1999_1999_subject_index_volume_2.pdf` â€” a journal subject index, not a paper. Probably should be removed from the bibliography entirely.
plan: Split the 35 unmatched PDFs into (a) duplicates of an already-linked file and (b) real papers missing from the bibliography. Add (b) to papers.bib, delete (a), then re-run bib_to_lab.py and expect unmatched to fall to zero. That count reaching zero is the falsifier for the bootstrap goal.

predictive_state.expected_behavior: Verified deterministic execution, schema alignment, and zero silent fallbacks.
